summary: Iteration 1 achieved a score of 94.82/100 on the 2D rectangular knapsack problem using a multi-strategy greedy packer (MaxRects with 6 orderings × 3 placement methods + skyline + randomized search). The remaining ~5% gap likely comes from suboptimal item-type ordering on specific test cases and fragmentation in near-prime bin dimensions.
key_points: Score of 94.82 was achieved with a type-level greedy MaxRects packer exploring 18+ deterministic strategies plus randomized perturbations within a 0.65s time budget — well above the initial 80+ target.

Key engineering lesson: expanding all item copies into a flat list (up to 24,000 candidates) causes TLE; iterating at the type level (place copies of one type until limit/no-fit, then next type) is essential for the 1-second time limit.

The ~5% gap is still unknown territory — it could be recoverable via local search (swap/remove/reinsert placements), better strip decomposition for awkward bin dimensions, or smarter item selection (e.g., solving a fractional knapsack to guide which types to prioritize before geometric packing).

Next iteration should investigate: (1) post-greedy local search (remove worst-profit items, repack freed space with higher-value alternatives), (2) a two-phase approach where a knapsack LP first selects target item counts, then a packer tries to realize that selection, and (3) more aggressive randomized restarts with tighter time management to explore more orderings.
